- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent history shows sustained upward momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >80% of forecasted values exceed true outcome by >5% in 3–5 consecutive days); apply a “cool-down” correction to reduce forecasted peak by 5–10%.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecasted values before final output.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecasted price exceeds 3σ above historical mean, reduce by 1–2σ; if below 3σ, increase by 1–2σ.
- Forecast horizon >10 days: model tends to underestimate true price; add 1–2% per day for lagged effects (e.g., +1.5% for 10-day forecast).
- Avoid overfitting to recent 5-day data; if last 5 days show strong upward trend, reduce forecasted peak by 3–5% to avoid overestimation.
